lines.text: One column of upper atmosphere. Ground below, space above.
Light is strongest at the top, and is used up on the way down.
Air does the opposite. It thickens downward, nearly tripling every scale height.
Multiply the two, one altitude at a time.
At the top: light, but no air. At the bottom: air, but no light.
The peak is the compromise. That is a Chapman layer.
Now let the Sun go down.
The peak climbs and it weakens. A low Sun gives a higher, thinner layer.
This is the shape a real daytime profile carries.
D, E and F1 are the same balance — different wavelengths, different gases.
At sunset production stops. D and E collapse in minutes: dense air, fast recombination.
That is why the shortwave bands go long after dark.
